questions.explanation: Framing updates the model's references to the current Delta version. Queries see data as of the last framing. 'Keep your Direct Lake data up to date' is on by default and reframes when changes are detected.

questions.sectionName: Mirroring, Direct Lake and Power BI
questions.question: What's the key behavioral difference between Direct Lake on OneLake and Direct Lake on SQL endpoints?
choices: Direct Lake on OneLake never falls back to DirectQuery; Direct Lake on SQL can fall back silently by default
Direct Lake on OneLake supports only import mode, while Direct Lake on SQL is live
Direct Lake on SQL can't use Delta tables, only Parquet files
They behave identically; the only difference is whether the model is stored in OneLake or in the SQL endpoint
questions.explanation: Direct Lake on OneLake is Microsoft's recommended mode for new models and runs in DirectLakeOnly. Direct Lake on SQL defaults to Automatic, which silently falls back to DirectQuery when it can't load from Delta. Silent fallback can make reports slow without anyone noticing.

questions.sectionName: Mirroring, Direct Lake and Power BI
questions.question: With DirectLakeBehavior set to DirectLakeOnly on a Direct Lake on SQL model, what happens when a query can't run in Direct Lake?
choices: The query fails with an error instead of falling back
It's queued until the next framing
It falls back to Import mode for that table
It silently falls back to DirectQuery for that one query
questions.explanation: DirectLakeBehavior has three values: Automatic (default, silent fallback), DirectLakeOnly (fail with an error) and DirectQueryOnly (always DirectQuery). Fallback triggers include SQL RLS, OLS or dynamic masking at the endpoint, tables over unmaterialized views, guardrail breaches, and stale framing.

questions.sectionName: Mirroring, Direct Lake and Power BI
questions.question: What are the Direct Lake guardrails on an F64 for rows per table and memory?
choices: 10 billion rows per table and 400 GB max memory
1.5 billion rows per table and 25 GB max memory (5,000 Parquet files and row groups)
Unlimited rows and unlimited memory
300 million rows per table and 3 GB max memory, the same limits as the smallest SKUs
questions.explanation: F64 guardrails: 5,000 Parquet files, 5,000 row groups, 1.5 billion rows per table, unlimited model size on disk, 25 GB max memory. F8 is 300 million rows, 10 GB model size and 3 GB memory. Large fact tables can force a bigger SKU, and one table over a guardrail blocks Direct Lake for the whole model.

questions.sectionName: Mirroring, Direct Lake and Power BI
questions.question: What happens when a Direct Lake on OneLake model exceeds a guardrail?
choices: Refresh fails, since that mode has no DirectQuery fallback
The model is automatically moved to a larger capacity
Only the affected visual shows an error; everything else is unaffected
Queries silently fall back to DirectQuery
questions.explanation: On Direct Lake on OneLake, exceeding a guardrail makes refresh fail. On Direct Lake on SQL, refresh succeeds with a warning and queries fall back if fallback is enabled. Know your largest tables' row counts before choosing an SKU.

questions.sectionName: Mirroring, Direct Lake and Power BI
questions.question: A team secured a lakehouse with SQL-endpoint row-level security, then built a Direct Lake on OneLake model. What happens?
choices: The model falls back to DirectQuery so the RLS is enforced
Queries succeed without the SQL-endpoint RLS; use OneLake security or model RLS instead
Queries fail until the RLS is removed from the SQL endpoint, because the two security models conflict
The SQL RLS is copied into the model automatically
questions.explanation: Microsoft: with Direct Lake on OneLake, queries succeed and SQL-based RLS isn't applied, because that mode isn't coupled to the SQL endpoint. It does work with OneLake security. On Direct Lake on SQL, endpoint RLS forces fallback or failure. Security must be enforced where the engine actually reads.

questions.sectionName: Mirroring, Direct Lake and Power BI
questions.question: Which data types or features does Direct Lake not support?
choices: Complex column types, binary and GUID columns, and model-defined partitions
Date and datetime columns
Integer and decimal columns, which must be converted to strings before framing
Delta tables with more than one Parquet file
questions.explanation: Direct Lake doesn't support complex types, binary and GUID types, NaN values or hybrid tables. Strings are capped at 32,764 characters, gateway refresh isn't supported, and model partitions aren't supported (Delta partitioning is). Wide JSON-ish tables from a lakehouse may need flattening first.

questions.sectionName: Mirroring, Direct Lake and Power BI
questions.question: When does a Direct Lake column get loaded into memory?
choices: Columns are never loaded; every query reads Parquet from disk
Every column loads at framing time, before any query
Only columns marked 'hot' by the admin load into memory
Only when a query first requests it, and it stays until evicted
questions.explanation: Transcoding loads columns on first use. They stay resident until a refresh picks up changes, they go unused for a while, or memory pressure evicts them. First-query latency after framing is normal behavior, not a bug.

questions.sectionName: Mirroring, Direct Lake and Power BI
questions.question: A Direct Lake on SQL model has a table built on a non-materialized SQL view. What happens to queries on it?
choices: The model refuses to publish until the view is removed
They run in Direct Lake normally, since views are just metadata
They fall back to DirectQuery (or fail, if fallback is disabled)
The view is materialized automatically during framing
questions.explanation: Tables over unmaterialized SQL views can't be read directly from Delta, so Direct Lake on SQL falls back. On Direct Lake on OneLake you can't use them at all, and Microsoft suggests lakehouse materialized views. Business logic kept in SQL views silently changes the performance profile.

questions.sectionName: Mirroring, Direct Lake and Power BI
questions.question: What does mirroring a database produce in Fabric, beyond the replicated Delta tables?
choices: A read-only SQL analytics endpoint, usable by Power BI Direct Lake and Spark
A writable copy of the source database that syncs changes back to the source
A Copilot Studio agent that answers questions about the data
A Power BI import model refreshed every 15 minutes
questions.explanation: Mirrored databases expose a read-only SQL analytics endpoint and Delta tables usable by Spark, SQL and Direct Lake. Writes still go to the source system. That makes mirroring a strong analytics-offload pattern, not a replacement for the operational database.

questions.sectionName: Mirroring, Direct Lake and Power BI
questions.question: Which mirroring source did Microsoft's mirroring overview mark as now generally available, with a banner?
choices: Teradata
Google BigQuery
Amazon Redshift
MongoDB Atlas
questions.explanation: The overview flags Google BigQuery mirroring as generally available, while Azure Database for MySQL, Dremio and SharePoint Lists are labeled preview. Release status varies by source and moves fast, so check before promising it to a customer.

questions.sectionName: Mirroring, Direct Lake and Power BI
questions.question: How much native Power BI storage does a Pro user get, compared with PPU?
choices: 10 GB per Pro user versus up to 100 TB for PPU
100 MB per Pro user and 1 GB for PPU
Unlimited for both, as storage moved to OneLake
1 TB per Pro user and 10 TB for PPU
questions.explanation: Power BI native storage is free up to 10 GB per Pro user and 100 TB for PPU. Import-model data in OneLake is included in the Power BI license price. Storage rarely decides the license on its own, but it adds up for heavy self-service users.

questions.sectionName: Mirroring, Direct Lake and Power BI
questions.question: Can Direct Lake models refresh through an on-premises data gateway?
choices: Yes. A gateway is required for every Direct Lake refresh, even for cloud sources
No. Direct Lake doesn't support gateway refresh; it uses cloud connections
Only VNet gateways, not on-premises ones
Only for tables larger than 1 billion rows
questions.explanation: Direct Lake works with cloud connections only and doesn't support gateway refresh. Microsoft recommends a fixed-identity cloud connection for model RLS and service principals. On-premises data must land in OneLake first, for example through mirroring or pipelines.

questions.sectionName: Mirroring, Direct Lake and Power BI
questions.question: What is DirectQuery in Power BI?
choices: A Fabric feature that replicates an operational database into OneLake in near real time, free of charge
A mode that copies data into the semantic model on each refresh, so queries are fast but are only as fresh as that copy
A mode that reads Delta tables in OneLake directly, loading the columns it needs into memory on demand
A mode that sends queries to the source system for every visual, so data is current but speed depends on the source
questions.explanation: DirectQuery queries the source live for every visual: data is always current, but performance depends on the source system. Import copies data into the model on refresh. Direct Lake reads Delta tables in OneLake directly, and Direct Lake on SQL can fall back to DirectQuery in some cases.

questions.sectionName: Mirroring, Direct Lake and Power BI
questions.question: Older Power BI documents talk about 'datasets'. What are they called now?
choices: Dataflows
Data agents
Warehouse tables
Semantic models
questions.explanation: Microsoft renamed Power BI datasets to semantic models. A semantic model holds the tables, relationships, measures and security that reports query. Fabric data agents can use semantic models as a source, and their row-level and column-level security still applies.

questions.sectionName: Mirroring, Direct Lake and Power BI
questions.question: A team wants Power BI reports over very large Delta tables in OneLake without keeping an imported copy and without DirectQuery's dependence on a source system. Which mode fits?
choices: Import mode with incremental refresh
Direct Lake
DirectQuery against the SQL endpoint
A composite model with dual storage
questions.explanation: Direct Lake reads Delta tables in OneLake directly and loads the columns it needs into memory on demand, so there's no imported copy to refresh. Each SKU has guardrails, and Direct Lake on SQL can fall back to DirectQuery when they're exceeded.

questions.sectionName: Mirroring, Direct Lake and Power BI
questions.question: A customer wants an Azure SQL database's data in OneLake within seconds of each change, at the lowest replication cost. Which option fits?
choices: A DirectQuery semantic model that reads the database live for every visual
Database mirroring, which replicates in near real time with free replication compute
A OneLake shortcut that points at the database's transaction log files
A nightly Copy job that reloads every table in full from the source database into a lakehouse
questions.explanation: Database mirroring replicates data into OneLake in near real time. The replication compute is free, and each capacity unit includes 1 TB of free mirroring storage. Querying the mirrored data still consumes capacity.

questions.sectionName: Mirroring, Direct Lake and Power BI
questions.question: How does data freshness differ between import mode and Direct Lake?
choices: Import is as fresh as the last data refresh; Direct Lake shows data as of the last framing
Both are always live, because Fabric pushes every change into the semantic model the moment it lands in OneLake
Import is refreshed by framing every few seconds; Direct Lake needs a full data refresh to see any new rows
Import always shows live data from the source; Direct Lake is as fresh as a nightly copy into the semantic model
questions.explanation: Import copies data into the model, so it's only as fresh as the last refresh. Direct Lake reads Delta files in OneLake, and framing, a cheap metadata-only refresh, points the model at the latest files. Queries see data as of the last framing.

questions.sectionName: Mirroring, Direct Lake and Power BI
questions.question: DirectQuery and Direct Lake both have 'Direct' in the name. What's the real difference?
choices: DirectQuery reads Delta files in OneLake into memory; Direct Lake sends each query to a source system
DirectQuery is for Fabric warehouses only; Direct Lake is for on-premises databases behind a gateway
DirectQuery sends each query to a source system; Direct Lake reads Delta files in OneLake into memory
They're the same mode: Direct Lake is the name DirectQuery took when Power BI moved into Fabric
questions.explanation: DirectQuery runs every visual's query against the source system live, so speed depends on the source. Direct Lake loads columns from Delta tables in OneLake into memory on demand. Direct Lake on SQL can fall back to DirectQuery when guardrails are exceeded, which is when the two meet.

questions.sectionName: Mirroring, Direct Lake and Power BI
questions.question: A Direct Lake report still shows yesterday's numbers, although the Delta table was updated an hour ago. What's the most likely cause?
choices: The report has fallen back to DirectQuery, which always lags a day behind the source
The semantic model hasn't been reframed since the update, so it still points at the older files
Direct Lake caches results for 24 hours, so new data appears only the following day
The table needs to be imported again, because Direct Lake can't see appended rows
questions.explanation: Direct Lake queries see data as of the last framing, a metadata-only refresh that points the model at the latest Delta files. If automatic updates are off or a refresh hasn't run since the load, the report shows older data. Check the model's refresh settings or trigger a refresh after loads.

questions.sectionName: Mirroring, Direct Lake and Power BI
questions.question: Some visuals in a Direct Lake on SQL report suddenly run much slower than the rest. What's a likely cause?
choices: The SQL endpoint switched those visuals to import mode until the next scheduled refresh
Those queries fell back to DirectQuery, for example after a guardrail was exceeded
Direct Lake on SQL reloads the whole table into memory every time a visual is used
The capacity paused framing for those tables to save CUs during busy hours
questions.explanation: Direct Lake on SQL can fall back to DirectQuery, for example when a table exceeds the SKU's guardrails or when SQL endpoint security requires it. Fallback queries run through the SQL endpoint and are slower. Direct Lake on OneLake can't fall back.

questions.sectionName: Mirroring, Direct Lake and Power BI
questions.question: What must be true of the data before a semantic model can use Direct Lake?
choices: It must be in Delta tables in OneLake
It must be imported into the model first
It must be in CSV files in SharePoint
It must be in an on-premises SQL Server
questions.explanation: Direct Lake reads Delta tables in OneLake, such as lakehouse or warehouse tables or mirrored data. Data elsewhere has to land in OneLake first, through pipelines, mirroring or shortcuts.

questions.sectionName: Mirroring, Direct Lake and Power BI
questions.question: A report author works in a workspace on an F64 capacity. What license do they need to publish and share reports?
choices: Power BI Pro or Premium Per User
None; F64 covers authors and viewers
A Fabric capacity admin role
A Microsoft 365 Copilot license
questions.explanation: F64 and larger lets free users view content, but building and sharing still needs Pro ($14) or PPU ($24). Plan author licenses even on large capacities.

questions.sectionName: Mirroring, Direct Lake and Power BI
questions.question: A customer mirrors 20 TB of data on an F16 capacity. How much mirroring storage is billed?
choices: None, because mirroring storage is always free
All 20 TB, because mirroring storage is never free
About 4 TB, because an F16 includes 16 TB free
About 18 TB, because only 2 TB is included
questions.explanation: Fabric includes 1 TB of free mirroring storage per capacity unit, so an F16 covers 16 TB and the remaining 4 TB is billed. Replication compute is free, but querying the mirrored data consumes capacity.

questions.question: What are Fabric's four workspace roles?
choices: Admin, Developer, Analyst and Consumer
Owner, Editor, Reader and Guest
Admin, Member, Contributor and Viewer
Capacity admin, Domain admin, Builder and Viewer
questions.explanation: Workspace roles can be assigned to users, security groups, Microsoft 365 groups, distribution lists and service principals. With multiple group memberships, the highest permission applies, so membership hygiene matters.

questions.question: A user has the Viewer role on a workspace with a lakehouse. How can they read its data?
choices: Only by downloading files from the Lakehouse explorer
Not at all. Viewers can only see reports, never data
Through Spark, the OneLake APIs and the SQL endpoint, exactly like any other workspace role
Only through the SQL analytics endpoint (T-SQL), not through Spark or the OneLake APIs
questions.explanation: All four roles can read lakehouse and warehouse data through the SQL endpoint (ReadData). Only Admin, Member and Contributor can read through Spark, the OneLake APIs and the Lakehouse explorer (ReadAll). Viewers also see no data in OneLake unless OneLake security roles grant it.

questions.question: Which workspace actions are reserved for the Admin role?
choices: Deleting the workspace, managing all membership including admins, creating a workspace identity and connecting to Git
Reading lakehouse data through Spark
Creating shortcuts and writing warehouse data
Running notebooks, scheduling pipeline refreshes and writing warehouse data, none of which Contributors or Members can do
questions.explanation: Admin-only actions include updating or deleting the workspace, adding or removing anyone (including admins), creating a workspace identity and connecting the workspace to Git. Contributors can create and modify most items and run jobs. Git connection being admin-only shapes how CI/CD is set up.

questions.question: Which workspace roles bypass OneLake security data-access roles?
choices: Only Viewer, because Viewers can't be assigned OneLake roles
None. OneLake security restricts every role equally
Admin, Member and Contributor, which already have read and write on all workspace data
Only Admin; Members and Contributors are restricted by OneLake security roles like everyone else
questions.explanation: Microsoft: Admins, Members and Contributors have read and write on all workspace data, so OneLake security roles don't affect them. They restrict only Viewers or users with item Read permission. For least privilege, give data consumers Viewer plus OneLake roles, not Contributor.

questions.question: What kinds of roles does OneLake security support?
choices: Grant-only roles: each grants access to specified data for its members, with no deny roles
Deny-only roles layered on top of workspace roles
Grant and deny roles, where a deny on any table or folder always takes precedence over grants
Roles defined only in Purview, not in Fabric
questions.explanation: OneLake security supports only Grant roles, each with permissions, data scope and members. Lakehouses include a DefaultReader role that gives ReadAll users access, which you can edit or delete. Without deny roles, scope grants carefully.

questions.question: A team creates one OneLake security role with row-level security and a separate role with column-level security, and assigns a user to both. What happens?
choices: It's unsupported and errors; RLS and CLS can be combined only within a single role
The most restrictive role wins
The most permissive of the two roles wins, so the user sees all rows and all columns
Both rules apply and are merged automatically
questions.explanation: RLS and CLS can be combined only inside a single role. Combining an RLS role with a separate CLS role is unsupported and errors. RLS also doesn't support dynamic or multi-table predicates. Unity Catalog's row filters, column masks and ABAC are more flexible here, a legitimate comparison point.

questions.question: Which engines enforce OneLake row- and column-level security?
choices: Only Power BI reports
Spark, the SQL analytics endpoint, semantic models and Power BI, plus authorized third-party engines (preview)
Only Spark notebooks enforce it today; SQL endpoints and Power BI ignore OneLake security until a future release
None yet; it's metadata only
questions.explanation: OneLake security is enforced across Spark, SQL endpoints, semantic models and Power BI, for Delta Parquet and virtualized Iceberg tables. Other table types are blocked for role members. Authorized third-party engines are in preview, and unauthorized ones are blocked from secured tables.

questions.question: Does assigning a workspace to a Fabric domain control who can access its data?
choices: No. Domains organize and delegate governance; access still comes from workspace roles and item permissions
Yes. Only members of a domain can open its workspaces, and domain membership replaces item-level sharing entirely
Yes. Domains replace workspace roles entirely
Only for workspaces on F64 or larger capacities
questions.explanation: Microsoft: domain assignment doesn't affect item visibility or accessibility. Domains group data by business area for discovery in the OneLake catalog and for delegated settings such as default sensitivity labels and certification. Don't sell domains as a security boundary.

questions.question: What can a Fabric domain admin not do?
choices: Assign workspaces to the domain
Edit the domain's description or change which workspaces belong to it
Change the domain's contributors
Delete or rename the domain, or add and remove other domain admins
questions.explanation: Fabric admins create domains and appoint domain admins. Domain admins can edit descriptions, contributors, workspace assignments and delegated overrides, but can't delete or rename the domain or manage other domain admins. Subdomains have no admins of their own.

questions.question: What does Microsoft Purview provide for Fabric?
choices: Capacity billing reports for Fabric
Only a data catalog scan of Fabric items, with no labeling, DLP, audit or insider risk features at all
Sensitivity labels on all Fabric items, DLP for structured data, audit, insider risk and AI governance
Encryption keys for OneLake, replacing customer-managed keys
questions.explanation: Purview adds Information Protection (labels on all items, persisting through supported export paths), DLP for lakehouses, warehouses, databases and semantic models, a full audit log, Insider Risk indicators, and support for Copilot and agents. The OneLake catalog is the primary in-Fabric governance experience.

questions.question: What does enabling tenant-level Private Link with 'Block Public Internet Access' do to Fabric?
choices: It turns on workspace-level customer-managed keys for every workspace
It moves the tenant to a sovereign cloud
Supported items become reachable only from private endpoints, and some features stop working
It encrypts all OneLake data with customer-managed keys and blocks all external guest users
questions.explanation: With Private Link and public access blocked, supported items are reachable only through private endpoints. Several features break: Copilot, the on-premises data gateway (use the VNet gateway), Publish to web, PDF and PowerPoint export, trial capacities, the Metrics app and Spark starter pools. That's a big tradeoff to surface early.

questions.question: A security team insists on tenant-level Private Link with public access blocked, and the business wants Copilot in Fabric. What's the conflict?
choices: Copilot works, but only on trial capacities
None. Copilot runs entirely inside the private endpoint like other Fabric features
Copilot isn't supported when tenant-level Private Link blocks public access
Copilot works, but only in Power BI Desktop
questions.explanation: Microsoft lists Copilot as unsupported with tenant-level Private Link and public access blocked. Workspace-level private links are the more granular alternative. Security posture and AI ambitions have to be reconciled up front.

questions.question: What is a Fabric workspace identity used for?
choices: A Purview label applied to every item in the workspace
The Git identity used to sign commits
A Fabric-managed service principal for trusted access to firewalled ADLS Gen2 and for connections
A personal account created for each workspace member so that their activity can be audited separately
questions.explanation: A workspace identity is an automatically managed service principal. It enables trusted workspace access to firewall-enabled ADLS Gen2 through shortcuts, and authentication for shortcuts, pipelines, semantic models and Dataflows Gen2. Trusted access requires a purchased F SKU.

questions.question: What happens if a workspace identity is deleted?
choices: It's moved to the recycle bin for 90 days
Nothing. Items fall back to the creator's identity
Dependent items break, and the deletion can't be undone, even if the workspace is restored
Fabric recreates it automatically within an hour, and dependent items reconnect on their own
questions.explanation: Deleting a workspace identity is permanent: dependent items break, and restoring the workspace doesn't restore the identity. Modifying the underlying Entra app also breaks it. Treat it like production credentials.

questions.question: Which items prevent a workspace from enabling customer-managed keys (CMK)?
choices: Notebooks and pipelines
Any unsupported item, including mirrored Azure Databricks catalogs and mirrored Dataverse
Lakehouses and warehouses, because CMK only supports notebooks, pipelines and SQL databases
SQL databases and Eventhouses
questions.explanation: Workspace CMK covers lakehouses, warehouses, notebooks, pipelines, SQL databases, Eventhouse (preview) and more, but a workspace with an unsupported item can't enable it. Mirrored Azure Databricks catalogs and mirrored Dataverse aren't supported. CMK needs an F SKU (not trial), and revoking the key makes reads and writes fail within 60 minutes.

questions.question: Which data is not protected by Fabric workspace CMK?
choices: Lakehouse Delta tables and warehouse tables, because CMK covers only metadata such as item names and descriptions
SQL database data files
Warehouse tables
Spark temp and shuffle data, environment libraries, pipeline metadata and the warehouse query cache
questions.explanation: CMK uses envelope encryption over OneLake data, but Spark cluster temp and shuffle data, libraries attached through environments, pipeline and copy job metadata, ML model metadata and the warehouse query cache aren't covered. Regulated customers should check this list against their requirements.

questions.question: Are Fabric tenant settings a security boundary?
choices: Only when combined with Private Link
Yes, but only for settings marked 'Security'
Yes. Tenant settings override every workspace role and item permission, which makes them the primary access control
No. Microsoft says they aren't a security measure; for example, 'Export data' doesn't restrict model read permission
questions.explanation: Microsoft states tenant settings aren't a security measure. They enable or disable features for groups and take up to 15 minutes to apply. Real access control comes from workspace roles, item permissions, OneLake security and labels.

questions.question: Which Fabric CI/CD tools does Microsoft document?
choices: Git integration (Azure DevOps or GitHub), deployment pipelines, variable libraries, the Fabric CLI and REST APIs
Only Terraform; Git isn't supported
Only Azure DevOps Classic Release pipelines
Only manual export and import of .pbix files between workspaces; Git and deployment pipelines aren't supported
questions.explanation: Fabric CI/CD combines Git integration, deployment pipelines (dev, test, prod with rules), variable libraries, deployment plans, the open-source Fabric CLI, REST APIs, a Terraform provider and the fabric-cicd Python library. Item support varies, so check before promising full automation.

questions.question: Which gateway works with tenant-level Private Link?
choices: Neither gateway type is supported
The VNet data gateway; the on-premises data gateway isn't supported
Any gateway, as long as it's in the same region
The on-premises data gateway only, installed on a server inside the VNet
questions.explanation: The on-premises gateway isn't supported with tenant-level Private Link, but the VNet data gateway works. Customers with on-premises sources must plan connectivity differently in a locked-down tenant.

questions.question: In a network-isolated environment, what does Microsoft note about Purview sensitivity labels in Power BI Desktop?
choices: Purview Information Protection doesn't support Private Link, so labeling and .pbix decryption can fail
Labels are converted to OneLake security roles
Desktop stops opening any file until labels are removed
Labels are enforced more strictly with Private Link on, so every protected file opens read-only in Desktop
questions.explanation: Purview Information Protection doesn't support Private Link. In isolated networks, Power BI Desktop's Sensitivity button is grayed out and decrypting protected .pbix files fails unless service tags allow it. Security features can conflict with each other.

questions.question: What stops trusted workspace access to a firewall-enabled storage account from working?
choices: Enabling soft delete on OneLake
Moving the workspace to a trial or non-F capacity
Adding more than ten members to the workspace at once
Using Direct Lake on OneLake
questions.explanation: Trusted workspace access requires a purchased F SKU. Migrating to a trial or non-F capacity stops it. Workspace identities also aren't supported across B2B or cross-tenant scenarios.

questions.question: What does OneLake security do with table formats other than Delta Parquet and virtualized Iceberg for users in a security role?
choices: It converts them to Delta automatically
It blocks those tables entirely for role members
It lets those tables through with no filtering at all
It applies only column security to them
questions.explanation: Row and column security are enforced for Delta Parquet and virtualized Iceberg tables. Other table types are blocked entirely for role members. Legacy formats in a lakehouse can vanish for restricted users once OneLake security is turned on.

questions.question: What is a domain in Fabric?
choices: A business grouping of workspaces, such as Finance, used for discovery and for delegating some settings
A network zone that keeps a set of workspaces behind their own private endpoint and firewall
A separate Fabric tenant for a business unit, with its own capacity, OneLake and admin portal
A security boundary that stops every user outside the domain from reading any of its workspaces' data at all
questions.explanation: Domains group workspaces by business area for discovery and for delegating some governance settings to domain admins. They don't control access: permissions still come from workspace roles, item permissions and OneLake security.

questions.question: A OneLake security role should hide some rows from an analyst, but the analyst still sees every row. The analyst is a Contributor in the workspace. Why?
choices: OneLake security applies only to Spark, so the analyst must be reading the table through the SQL endpoint
Row-level rules take up to 24 hours to apply, so the role will start working tomorrow for every user
Admins, Members and Contributors bypass OneLake security, which restricts only Viewers and readers
OneLake security works only on Iceberg tables, so the Delta table has to be converted before rules apply
questions.explanation: OneLake security roles are grant-only and are enforced across Spark, SQL endpoints, semantic models and Power BI, but workspace Admins, Members and Contributors bypass them. Give read-only users the Viewer role, or item Read permission, so the rules apply.

questions.question: After an admin enables tenant-level Private Link, refreshes through the on-premises data gateway start failing. What's the fix?
choices: Reinstall the on-premises gateway on a server in the capacity's Azure region
Turn on cross-geo processing so that the gateway can reach Fabric over the public internet as before
Use a VNet data gateway; the on-premises gateway doesn't work with tenant-level Private Link
Move the semantic models to a trial capacity, which skips Private Link checks
questions.explanation: The on-premises data gateway doesn't work with tenant-level Private Link, but the VNet data gateway does. Tenant-level Private Link with public access blocked also turns off several features, Copilot among them, so review the list before enabling it.

questions.question: Which of these beliefs about Fabric governance is a myth?
choices: Turning a feature off in tenant settings is a security boundary
Tenant setting changes can take up to 15 minutes to apply
Workspace Contributors bypass OneLake security roles
Domains group workspaces but don't control access to them
questions.explanation: Microsoft says tenant settings aren't a security boundary: they turn features on for everyone or chosen groups. The other three statements are true. Security comes from workspace roles, item permissions, OneLake security and network controls.

questions.question: What does a workspace need before it can use customer-managed keys in Fabric?
choices: A Power BI Premium P SKU and a key stored in OneLake
To sit on an F SKU capacity, with the key kept in Azure Key Vault
An F64 or larger and a key in Microsoft-managed storage
Any capacity, including trials, plus a Purview license
questions.explanation: Fabric supports customer-managed keys for workspaces on F SKUs only, with the key in Azure Key Vault. Revoking the key cuts off access to the data, so the key's lifecycle becomes an operational responsibility.

questions.question: What capacity does Copilot in Fabric need?
choices: No capacity; Copilot in Fabric is licensed per user like Microsoft 365 Copilot
Any capacity, including trial
F64 or higher only
A paid Fabric capacity of F2 or higher, or Power BI Premium P1 or higher
questions.explanation: Copilot is enabled by default for tenants with paid F2+ capacities, and also works on P1+. Pro and PPU workspaces aren't directly supported, and trial SKUs don't get Azure OpenAI. The old F64 minimum is gone, but small capacities can throttle under AI load.

questions.question: Is Copilot in Fabric licensed per user, like Microsoft 365 Copilot?
choices: Yes, it's included only with Power BI PPU
It's billed in Copilot Credits per prompt
Yes. Every Fabric Copilot user needs a $30 Microsoft 365 Copilot license assigned to them
No. It consumes the Fabric capacity's CUs; there's no per-user Copilot in Fabric license
questions.explanation: Copilot in Fabric runs on capacity: 100 CU-seconds per 1,000 input tokens and 400 per 1,000 output tokens, billed to the content's capacity or a designated Fabric Copilot capacity. Copilot in Power BI Desktop consumes the selected workspace's capacity. Don't confuse it with the Microsoft 365 Copilot seat.

questions.question: A UK customer's Fabric capacity is in UK South. What must the admin enable for Copilot to work?
choices: Nothing. Azure OpenAI is hosted in every Fabric region
A Private Link from UK South to the EU Data Boundary, since Copilot can't reach Azure OpenAI over the internet
The tenant setting allowing processing outside the capacity's geography, since UK requests go to the EU
A Microsoft 365 Copilot license for each user
questions.explanation: Azure OpenAI for Fabric is hosted in the US and the EU Data Boundary. UK capacities process in the EU, and many other geographies (Australia, Canada, India, Japan and more) process in the US, so the cross-geo processing tenant setting must be enabled. That's a residency decision for the customer's DPO.

questions.question: Which Fabric experiences include Copilot?
choices: Only notebooks
Only the Fabric admin portal
Notebooks, Data Factory, Data Warehouse, SQL database, Power BI and Real-Time Intelligence
Only Power BI reports and dashboards, because other Fabric workloads don't include Copilot yet
questions.explanation: Copilot appears across notebooks, Data Factory, Warehouse, SQL database, Power BI (Desktop and apps) and Real-Time Intelligence (KQL querysets and dashboards). Admins can control Copilot at the workload level but not per experience, and sovereign clouds aren't supported.

questions.question: What do Fabric admins control through Copilot tenant settings?
choices: The model version, temperature and maximum tokens that each workspace's Copilot uses, set per capacity by the Fabric admin
A per-user monthly token budget for Copilot
Which Microsoft 365 Copilot licenses apply to Fabric
Who can use Azure OpenAI and OpenAI-powered features, and whether data may leave the capacity's geography
questions.explanation: There are four tenant settings: use of Azure OpenAI features, cross-geo processing for Azure OpenAI, use of OpenAI as a Microsoft subprocessor (Copilot, AI agents), and cross-geo processing for that. Each can be scoped to security groups and delegated to capacity admins.

questions.question: How many data sources can a Fabric data agent combine, and which types?
choices: Up to 50 sources of any type, including PDF and Word documents in lakehouse Files folders and SharePoint libraries
Unlimited, but only from one workspace
Up to five: lakehouses, warehouses, KQL databases, Power BI semantic models, ontologies and Microsoft Graph
One, which must be a semantic model
questions.explanation: Data agents (GA) answer from up to five structured sources, read-only, with results capped at 25 rows and 25 columns. They're English only, the LLM can't be changed, and there's no unstructured data. They query with the requesting user's identity.

questions.question: Which tenant setting must be on for Fabric data agents to work?
choices: Cross-geo processing and storing for AI
External sharing to anyone
Publish to web for the whole organization
Allow Pro workspaces on capacity
questions.explanation: Data agents require the tenant setting that allows cross-geo processing and storing for AI, plus a paid F2+ or P1+ capacity. They aren't supported on trial capacities.

questions.question: Where are Fabric data agent responses processed when the agent is used from Microsoft 365 Copilot?
choices: They may be processed outside Fabric's compliance boundary or geographic region, as Microsoft warns
Always inside the capacity's own region with no exceptions, as with any other Fabric workload today
Only on the user's device
Inside the Databricks workspace that holds the data
questions.explanation: Microsoft warns that responses used through Microsoft 365 Copilot and Copilot Studio may leave Fabric's compliance boundary or region. Each hop in an agent chain is a data flow to document.

questions.question: What is a Fabric Copilot capacity?
choices: A capacity that runs only Microsoft 365 Copilot
A per-user Copilot license for Fabric
A designated capacity that absorbs Copilot and data agent usage for chosen users instead of the content's capacity
A free capacity that Microsoft provides for AI features, so Copilot usage never counts against paid capacity at all
questions.explanation: Fabric Copilot capacity (minimum F2 or P1, home region only) bills selected users' Copilot and data agent usage to one capacity. It's good for chargeback and for protecting production capacity. Each user maps to one Copilot capacity, and the most recently created one wins.

questions.question: What was the status of Fabric IQ integrations in Microsoft Copilot after Ignite 2026?
choices: Generally available, while Fabric IQ in Excel and the ChatGPT and Claude connectors were in preview
Retired in favor of Fabric data agents, which now cover every scenario Fabric IQ used to support in Copilot
Private preview for Frontier customers only
Available only in sovereign clouds
questions.explanation: Per the Book of News, Fabric IQ integrations in Microsoft Copilot are GA. Fabric IQ in Excel, connectors for ChatGPT and Claude, ontologies in GitHub Copilot, and IQ sharing for ontologies are in preview. Microsoft IQ (Work IQ, Fabric IQ, Foundry IQ) came with no new SKU.

questions.question: When an analyst uses Copilot in Power BI Desktop, which capacity pays?
choices: The analyst's Microsoft 365 Copilot license, so no capacity is used
The tenant's largest capacity automatically
The capacity of the workspace the analyst selects for Copilot
Nothing. Desktop Copilot is free
questions.explanation: Copilot in Power BI Desktop consumes the selected workspace's capacity. Point Desktop Copilot at a development or Copilot capacity, not the production capacity serving executive dashboards.

questions.question: A Fabric data agent's results feel truncated for a detailed list request. Why?
choices: Copilot hides rows the user isn't licensed to see
Semantic models return only their top 25 measures
The capacity is throttled to 25 rows during business hours
Data agent responses are capped at 25 rows and 25 columns
questions.explanation: The 25 × 25 cap is by design. Data agents give answers, not extracts. For detailed lists, point users to a report, or compare with Genie Agents, which support up to 50 tables and richer analytical answers.

questions.question: How do Fabric data agents enforce semantic model security?
choices: They apply the creator's RLS role to everyone
They require turning RLS off before publishing
They ignore RLS, so data agents should only ever be built on non-sensitive data
They query as the requesting user, so semantic model RLS and CLS still apply
questions.explanation: Data agents use the requesting user's identity, and for semantic models RLS and CLS still apply (Read permission needed, Build not). That's the same principle Genie follows with Unity Catalog, so both can be governed in a comparable way.

questions.question: Is Copilot in Fabric available on a trial capacity?
choices: Only during the first 7 days of the trial
No. Azure OpenAI isn't available on trial SKUs
Yes, with the same features as F64
Yes, but limited to Power BI
questions.explanation: Trials don't support Copilot or AI experiences (data agents, AI functions), so a Fabric AI proof of concept needs paid capacity. An F2 is enough to start.

questions.question: A Copilot request in Fabric uses 2,000 input and 500 output tokens. Using Microsoft's rates, how many CU-seconds does it consume?
choices: 400 CU-seconds (200 for input + 200 for output)
2,500 CU-seconds, at one CU-second per token used
4,000 CU-seconds
40 CU-seconds
questions.explanation: Input: 2 × 100 = 200. Output: 0.5 × 400 = 200. Total 400 CU-seconds, which matches Microsoft's own example. An F2 has 60 CU-seconds per 30-second timepoint, so a few heavy Copilot users can push small capacities into smoothing debt, even though it runs as a background job.

questions.question: Can Copilot in Fabric be turned on or off per individual experience, such as only in notebooks?
choices: No. Control is at the workload level, not per experience
Only for Power BI, which has a separate switch per report
Yes. Each experience has its own tenant switch
Yes, but only through PowerShell
questions.explanation: Copilot can't be enabled per experience. Control sits at the workload and tenant-setting level, scoped to security groups. Granular governance means choosing which groups get Copilot, not which features.

questions.question: In Fabric IQ, what is an ontology?
choices: A model of business entities and how they relate, such as customers and orders, that agents use to read questions
A Purview classification scheme that labels each column as public, internal or confidential before AI can use it
A Copilot setting that picks which language model answers questions in each Fabric workload, set per capacity
A list of approved data sources that a Fabric data agent may query, kept by the Fabric administrator for each domain
questions.explanation: An ontology describes business entities and their relationships so agents interpret questions the way the business does. Fabric IQ uses ontologies alongside planning, Fabric Graph and semantic models. Databricks' Genie Ontology is a comparable context layer that's built automatically.

questions.question: What role does Azure OpenAI play in Copilot in Fabric?
choices: None: Copilot in Fabric runs its own Microsoft-trained models inside each customer's Fabric capacity region
It hosts Copilot in Fabric's models in US and EU regions, so other regions need cross-geo processing
It stores Copilot conversation history for 30 days so that admins can review prompts and responses later
It's an optional add-on that customers buy per user to make Copilot in Fabric answer in more languages
questions.explanation: Copilot in Fabric uses Azure OpenAI models hosted in US and EU regions. Capacities in other geographies need the tenant setting that allows cross-geo processing, which makes turning Copilot on a data residency decision as well as a feature one.

questions.question: A customer says, 'Copilot in Fabric needs an F64, so we can't afford it.' What's accurate?
choices: That's right: Copilot in Fabric needs an F64 or larger, and it isn't available on smaller capacities at all
Copilot in Fabric needs no capacity, because it's licensed through Microsoft 365 Copilot seats instead
The F64 minimum is gone: paid F2 or larger (or P1+) works, though small capacities can throttle
It works on any capacity, including trials, as long as each user has a Power BI Pro license
questions.explanation: Copilot in Fabric works on paid F2+ capacities and P1+, so the old F64 minimum no longer applies. It isn't available on trial capacities. On small capacities, a few heavy users can push the capacity into smoothing debt, so size with a pilot.

questions.question: A sales rep asks a Fabric data agent in Teams about revenue. The agent uses a semantic model with row-level security. Which rows can the rep get?
choices: Only the rows the rep's own row-level security allows, because the agent queries as the rep
Every row, because Teams requests bypass semantic model security altogether
Every row, because the agent queries with its creator's permissions for all users
No rows, because data agents can't use semantic models with row-level security
questions.explanation: A Fabric data agent queries read-only with the asking user's identity, so the semantic model's row-level and column-level security still apply. Two reps asking the same question can get different answers, and that's the design working.

questions.question: A user assigned to a Fabric Copilot capacity uses Copilot on a report in a workspace that sits on a different capacity. Which capacity pays for the Copilot usage?
choices: Neither, because Copilot is billed to the user's seat
The capacity that holds the report's workspace
The Fabric Copilot capacity the user is assigned to
Both, split evenly between the two capacities
questions.explanation: A Fabric Copilot capacity absorbs Copilot and data agent usage for chosen users instead of billing the capacity that holds the content. It's useful for chargeback and for protecting production capacity. Each user maps to one Copilot capacity, and the minimum size is F2 or P1.

questions.question: 50 users each make 20 Copilot in Fabric requests a day, each with about 1,000 input and 250 output tokens. At 100 CU-seconds per 1,000 input tokens and 400 per 1,000 output tokens, roughly how many CUs does that average over a day?
choices: About 2.3 CUs, more than an F2 provides
About 23 CUs, which needs an F32
About 0.2 CUs, a tenth of an F2
None, because Copilot doesn't use CUs
questions.explanation: Each request uses 100 + 100 = 200 CU-seconds, so 50 × 20 × 200 = 200,000 CU-seconds a day. Spread over 86,400 seconds, that's about 2.3 CUs on average, more than an F2's 2. Copilot can tip a small capacity into throttling, so size from a pilot or use a Fabric Copilot capacity.

questions.question: When a Unity Catalog catalog is mirrored into Fabric, how does Fabric access the table data?
choices: By exporting tables to Parquet through Delta Sharing each hour
By running queries on the Databricks SQL warehouse for every request
Through OneLake shortcuts to the existing Delta files; only metadata is synchronized
By copying every table into OneLake nightly, through a pipeline that Fabric manages
questions.explanation: Mirroring an Azure Databricks catalog syncs the catalog structure and reads data through shortcuts, with no data movement. Fabric creates a mirrored item and a read-only SQL analytics endpoint, and Power BI can use Direct Lake against it. Queries then run on Fabric capacity, not Databricks.

questions.question: A mirrored Unity Catalog catalog in Fabric shows fewer tables than the Databricks catalog. Which are documented reasons?
choices: Tables larger than 1 TB are skipped automatically, so the mirrored catalog stays within the free mirroring storage allowance
Tables owned by service principals are hidden from Fabric users
Tables with row filters or column masks, views and metric views, and federated and Delta Sharing tables aren't mirrored
Only tables created in the last 90 days are mirrored
questions.explanation: Fabric's limitations exclude tables with RLS or column-masking policies, views, metric views, lakehouse federated tables and Delta Sharing tables, and non-Delta external tables aren't shown. The governed and semantic assets (policies, metric views) are what don't carry over. That's the core reason to keep consumption on Genie and Unity Catalog where governance holds.

questions.question: What does mirroring Unity Catalog into Fabric require at the storage layer?
choices: The storage account must first be copied into a Fabric-managed Azure subscription
The ADLS Gen2 account behind the Databricks tables must be reachable by Fabric
Disabling the storage firewall entirely
Converting tables from Delta to Iceberg first
questions.explanation: Because Fabric reads through shortcuts, it needs network access to the underlying ADLS Gen2 account. That's a second path to the data outside Unity Catalog's enforcement, so it should be part of the security review. Workspace identity and trusted workspace access can help with firewalled storage.

questions.question: How quickly do Unity Catalog schema changes appear in a mirrored catalog in Fabric?
choices: Once a day at midnight UTC
Only after a manual resync by a Fabric admin
Instantly, inside the same transaction
Anywhere from a few seconds to several minutes
questions.explanation: Metadata sync is on by default but not instantaneous: Microsoft says propagation takes seconds to several minutes. Mirrored catalogs also can't live in CMK-enabled workspaces, a constraint for regulated customers.

questions.question: What does OneLake catalog federation let Azure Databricks do?
choices: Query Fabric lakehouse and warehouse data in place on Databricks compute, read-only and without copying
Write directly into Fabric warehouses with full DML, running the queries on Fabric capacity instead of Databricks
Run Databricks notebooks on Fabric capacity
Copy OneLake tables into Unity Catalog managed storage nightly
questions.explanation: OneLake catalog federation creates a foreign catalog in Unity Catalog over a Fabric Lakehouse or Warehouse. Queries run on Databricks compute and read OneLake data with zero copy. It's read-only (SELECT only), so Databricks can be the governed AI and BI layer even over data that lives in Fabric.

questions.question: What identity does Azure Databricks use to read OneLake through catalog federation?
choices: An Access Connector managed identity (recommended) or a service principal, not end-user passthrough
Anonymous access, since federation is read-only
Each Databricks user's own Fabric credentials, passed through so OneLake checks every individual user
A Fabric workspace identity created by Databricks automatically
questions.explanation: Federation authenticates to Fabric as a managed identity or service principal. Per-user access is then governed in Unity Catalog (USE CATALOG, USE SCHEMA, SELECT). On the Fabric side, the SQL-only 'Read all with SQL analytics endpoint' permission isn't enough; use 'Read all with Apache Spark' or broader. Cross-tenant setups need a service principal.

questions.question: Which is a documented limitation of OneLake catalog federation?
choices: No complex types, no views or materialized views, and no dedicated access mode
It requires every Fabric workspace to be on F64 or above
It's limited to 10 queries per minute per workspace
It only works for tables under 1 GB, so larger lakehouse tables must be split first
questions.explanation: Limits include read-only SELECT access, Lakehouse and Warehouse items only, Databricks Runtime 18.0+ in standard access mode (SQL warehouses 2025.40+), no complex types, no views or materialized views, and connection options that can't change after creation. Cross-region reads incur data transfer charges, so keep both in the same region.

questions.question: Which Fabric tenant settings does OneLake catalog federation require?
choices: Publish to web, external sharing with anyone, and Copilot cross-geo processing, all enabled for the whole organization
Allow Copilot cross-geo processing
Service principals calling Fabric APIs, external apps accessing OneLake, and short-lived user-delegated SAS tokens
Block public internet access
questions.explanation: Federation needs three tenant settings plus the workspace setting 'Authenticate with OneLake user-delegated SAS tokens'. Locked-down tenants often have these off, so involve the Fabric admin early in any 'Databricks reads Fabric data' design.

questions.question: A Power BI report uses Direct Lake over a mirrored Unity Catalog catalog. Which platform's compute serves the report queries?
choices: Fabric capacity (CUs); Databricks compute isn't involved in serving those queries
Databricks SQL warehouse DBUs, because the underlying data still lives in Databricks storage
Neither. Direct Lake queries are free
Both platforms, billed twice per query
questions.explanation: With mirroring plus Direct Lake, Fabric reads the Delta files through shortcuts and serves queries on its own capacity. Workload moves from Databricks DBUs to Fabric CUs, and Unity Catalog row filters and masks aren't in the path. Make that compute and governance shift explicit when the customer compares options.

questions.question: When Databricks queries Fabric data through OneLake catalog federation, whose compute does the work?
choices: The Fabric SQL analytics endpoint, billed in CUs
Azure Databricks compute; Fabric isn't copying or serving the data
Fabric capacity, billed in CUs to the workspace that owns the lakehouse
A shared Microsoft–Databricks pool billed to neither
questions.explanation: Federated queries run on Databricks compute and read OneLake files in place. OneLake read transactions may still register on the Fabric side, and cross-region reads add transfer charges. The direction of the integration decides who pays.

questions.question: What did Microsoft announce in 2026 about Unity Catalog and OneLake storage?
choices: OneLake will no longer accept Delta tables written by Databricks
Databricks must copy all tables into Fabric warehouses to share them
Unity Catalog is being replaced by the OneLake catalog for every Azure Databricks customer starting in 2027
Azure Databricks can store Unity Catalog managed tables in OneLake, read by Fabric via a mirrored catalog
questions.explanation: Microsoft's Fabric blog announced that Azure Databricks can store Unity Catalog managed tables directly in OneLake. Unity Catalog stays the governing catalog on the Databricks side, and Fabric users read through a mirrored catalog item. One copy of the data, two engines: the open-lakehouse story both vendors now tell.

questions.question: How can Azure Databricks data get into the Power BI service without mirroring?
choices: Only through Fabric mirroring, because Power BI has no direct connector to Azure Databricks clusters or warehouses
Publish datasets from Databricks to Power BI, or connect Power BI Desktop to a cluster or SQL warehouse
Only by exporting CSV files to SharePoint
Only by rebuilding the tables in a Fabric warehouse
questions.explanation: Databricks supports Publish to Power BI and the Power BI Desktop connector to clusters and SQL warehouses, with OAuth or service principal setups. Connecting Unity Catalog metric views to Power BI is in private preview. In this path, queries run on Databricks compute with Unity Catalog permissions in force.

questions.question: A customer wants governed self-service BI over Databricks data for 3,000 viewers and is choosing between an F32 and an F64. What's the key licensing fact?
choices: Below F64, every viewer needs Pro or PPU; at F64+ free users can view, which changes the cost comparison
F32 and F64 have identical Power BI licensing rules
Viewers never need any Power BI license on a Fabric capacity of any size, as long as they view in Teams
Viewers need Microsoft 365 Copilot licenses on F32
questions.explanation: At $14 per Pro user, 3,000 viewers is $42,000 a month on top of an F32. F64 lets free users view. Work out the true cost (capacity, Pro seats, storage, the Databricks compute behind it) and compare with alternatives such as Databricks AI/BI dashboards and Genie for consumption.

questions.question: A customer's data platform team runs everything on Databricks with Unity Catalog row filters. The BI team proposes mirroring into Fabric for Direct Lake reports. What's the strongest governance concern?
choices: Fabric caps mirrored catalogs at 100 report users unless the capacity is F128 or larger
Direct Lake can't read Delta tables created by Databricks
Mirroring copies every Delta table into OneLake a second time, so storage doubles and the copies drift from the source within hours
Policy-protected tables won't mirror, and Fabric access bypasses Unity Catalog, creating a second governance model
questions.explanation: Mirroring is metadata plus shortcuts (no double storage), and Direct Lake reads Delta fine. But policy-protected tables are excluded, and whatever is mirrored is governed by Fabric permissions, not Unity Catalog. Options: keep consumption on Databricks (Genie, AI/BI dashboards, Power BI DirectQuery with Unity Catalog), or deliberately re-implement security in OneLake security and semantic-model RLS, accepting two places to manage policy.

questions.question: When is Fabric arguably the better fit than adding Databricks, to give fair, credible coaching?
choices: When Unity Catalog row filters and ABAC must govern every access path
When data lives across AWS, GCP and Azure and must stay in place
For Power BI-centric teams with modest data volumes and SQL skills who want one SaaS bill and Direct Lake reporting
When the customer needs advanced ML, streaming at massive scale and multi-cloud portability across AWS and GCP
questions.explanation: Fabric's strengths are a unified SaaS experience, Power BI integration (Direct Lake), T-SQL warehousing, low-friction mirroring and F2 entry pricing. Databricks tends to win on advanced data engineering and ML, open multi-cloud governance, fine-grained policy and agentic analytics with Genie. Acknowledging where Fabric fits makes the rest of your advice more credible.

questions.question: A customer plans to pause its F64 every night to save money, and it has database mirroring running from Azure SQL. What breaks?
choices: Nothing, because mirroring runs on Microsoft's free replication compute whether or not the capacity is running at all
The mirrored tables are deleted and must be re-seeded each morning
Mirroring stops replicating while paused, and mirrored storage is billed as regular OneLake storage during the pause
Only Power BI refreshes are affected; mirroring is unaffected
questions.explanation: A running capacity is required for mirroring, and pausing stops replication. Storage that was free under the mirroring allowance is billed while paused, and pausing also bills accumulated smoothed usage. Night pausing can still make sense, but model the side effects first.

questions.question: Do Fabric capacity and Azure Databricks consumption compete for a customer's Azure MACC?
choices: Only Databricks counts toward MACC; Fabric is Microsoft 365 spend
Neither counts toward MACC
Both are Azure spend that burns down the same MACC, so MACC isn't a reason to pick one over the other
Only Fabric counts toward MACC, because Azure Databricks is billed as a third-party marketplace charge
questions.explanation: Fabric F SKUs are MACC-eligible, and Azure Databricks is a first-party Azure service billed through the customer's subscription. Steer the decision to capability, governance and total cost rather than which product burns down the commitment.

questions.question: A customer wants one semantic definition of revenue used by both Power BI and AI agents. What's the tradeoff between Unity Catalog metric views and Power BI semantic models?
choices: Metric views are mirrored into Fabric automatically as Power BI semantic models, so one definition serves both platforms
There's no tradeoff; both platforms read each other's semantic layers fully
Power BI semantic models can be queried by Genie natively today
Metric views govern metrics for Genie and SQL, but don't mirror to Fabric, and their Power BI link is in private preview
questions.explanation: Unity Catalog metric views give a governed semantic layer for Genie, dashboards and SQL, but they don't appear in mirrored catalogs, and the Power BI connection to them is in private preview. Power BI semantic models serve Power BI and Fabric data agents. Choose deliberately where the 'golden' definition lives, and avoid two that drift apart.

questions.question: A customer's Fabric security relies on workspace Contributor roles for analysts who only need to read curated data. What should you recommend?
choices: Use Viewer plus OneLake security roles (or item permissions), since Contributors bypass OneLake security and can write
Use domains to restrict which tables they can see
Keep them as Contributors, because that's the least-privileged role able to read lakehouse data through every engine
Make them Admins so they can manage their own access
questions.explanation: Contributors can read and write all workspace data and aren't restricted by OneLake security roles. Least privilege means Viewer (SQL endpoint read) plus OneLake roles for Spark and OneLake access, or item-level sharing. Domains don't control access. The same principle applies in Unity Catalog: grant what's needed, at the data layer.

questions.question: A customer in a network-isolated tenant wants Databricks to read Fabric lakehouses through catalog federation. What networking detail matters on newer Databricks runtimes?
choices: Federation requires disabling Private Link on both sides
Runtime 19+ uses per-workspace OneLake endpoints, so firewall rules written for the global endpoint may need updating
Databricks must be moved into the Fabric tenant's VNet
Federation works only over the public internet, so the firewalls on both platforms must be fully disabled before setup
questions.explanation: From Databricks Runtime 19, federation uses per-workspace endpoints (<workspace-id>.z<xy>.dfs.fabric.microsoft.com), so firewall allow-lists for the global endpoint may need changes. Workspaces that block public access need a resource instance rule (same tenant) or a private endpoint (cross-tenant).

questions.question: When is mirroring a Unity Catalog catalog into Fabric the wrong choice for a set of tables?
choices: When the tables rely on row filters or column masks, because those tables aren't mirrored
When the tables are stored as Delta, because Fabric can only mirror plain Parquet files today
When the tables are updated daily, because mirroring only supports weekly syncs
When the tables are larger than 1 TB, because mirroring is capped at that size
questions.explanation: Tables with row filters or column masks aren't mirrored, and neither are views or metric views. Mirrored data is also governed by Fabric, not Unity Catalog. For governed, per-user data, query it through Databricks, for example with Genie or a Databricks SQL connection from Power BI.

questions.question: Mirroring an Azure Databricks catalog and OneLake catalog federation both connect Fabric and Databricks. How do they differ?
choices: Mirroring brings Unity Catalog tables into Fabric; catalog federation lets Databricks query Fabric data in place
They're the same feature: Microsoft calls it mirroring and Databricks calls it catalog federation
Mirroring lets Databricks query Fabric data in place; catalog federation brings Unity Catalog tables into Fabric
Both copy data in both directions every night, but only catalog federation keeps Unity Catalog permissions
questions.explanation: A mirrored Azure Databricks catalog is a Fabric item that mirrors a Unity Catalog catalog's metadata and reads its Delta files through shortcuts; access in Fabric is governed by Fabric. OneLake catalog federation goes the other way: Databricks exposes Fabric lakehouses and warehouses as a read-only foreign catalog in Unity Catalog.

questions.question: After mirroring a Unity Catalog catalog into Fabric, several tables and all the metric views are missing. What's the likely explanation?
choices: The workspace's capacity is too small, so Fabric dropped the largest tables first
Mirroring copies only tables created in the last 90 days, so older tables are skipped
Tables with row filters or column masks, views and metric views aren't mirrored
Fabric mirrors one schema at a time, and the others are still waiting in the queue
questions.explanation: The Azure Databricks mirroring limitations list tables with row filters or column masks, views and metric views among the things that aren't mirrored. Check which tables rely on Unity Catalog security or semantics before promising a Fabric experience over them.

questions.question: A customer says, 'We'll move everything from Databricks to Fabric so we only have one copy of the data.' Which reply is accurate and doesn't overclaim?
choices: Databricks can't read anything stored in OneLake, so the customer would lose all of its Databricks pipelines on day one
Fabric can't read Delta tables at all, so moving would mean keeping two copies of every table in two formats forever
Mirroring keeps every Unity Catalog row filter and column mask in force in Fabric, so nothing about governance changes
Both store Delta on open storage, so they can share one copy without migrating; governance differs by engine
questions.explanation: Delta Lake is the default table format in both platforms, which is why they can share one copy: Fabric can mirror Unity Catalog, and Databricks can federate OneLake. Governance follows the engine doing the reading, though, and tables with row filters or column masks aren't mirrored. The other replies overclaim.

questions.question: A Power BI report uses Direct Lake over a mirrored Azure Databricks catalog. Which permissions decide who can read the data?
choices: Unity Catalog's, because mirroring carries every grant, filter and mask across into Fabric
Fabric's, because access through Fabric is governed by Fabric rather than Unity Catalog
Both, because Fabric checks Unity Catalog grants again on each query it serves
Only Power BI row-level security, because Direct Lake skips other Fabric permissions
questions.explanation: A mirrored Azure Databricks catalog mirrors metadata and reads Unity Catalog's Delta files through shortcuts, and access through Fabric is governed by Fabric, not Unity Catalog. That's why tables relying on Unity Catalog row filters or column masks aren't mirrored. Plan Fabric permissions as a second governance layer.
